title: autopilot step 4 of the ledger removal: restack keeps one record per PR head instead of a once() ledger entry, and fm-restack says why it refused through distinct exit statuses (rebase conflict, GitHub head moved, stale local ref, published but unfinished, live worker)
acceptance: Why. `restack()` (bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:393-403) still runs `fm-restack.sh` through the write-ahead `once()` ledger: `self.once(['restack', number, head, parent], task, lambda: self.command(...))`. Any failure, and any interruption, parks that token 'uncertain' and wakes firstmate, and the same head is never retried, even when the failure was transient. The helper itself cannot say why it refused: bin/lib/fm_stack.py raises one `ValueError` for every refusal and `main()` exits 65 for all of them (:197-199), so a head that GitHub moved (:72-73, :102-103), a stale local task ref (:72-73, `rev-parse refs/heads/<branch>`), a live worker (:184-189), a rebase conflict (:98, the `git rebase --onto` call) and a failure after the push already published (:116-127) are indistinguishable. A stale local branch therefore parks the same way as a remote move. This is step L2 of the ledger removal (state/briefs/PLAN-2026-10-05-remaining-issues.md item 4, after T-190 update, T-193 advance and T-200 pr-event/recheck).

Distinct refusals in bin/lib/fm_stack.py. Add six `ValueError` subclasses (so `assertRaises(ValueError)`-style tests that do not reach the rebase keep passing; the two that do are changed, see Tests) and raise them where the case is known:
- `RestackMoved`: GitHub's head for the child is not `expected` (split :72-73 so this check runs first, on `child['headRefOid']` from `remote_head`), and 'child moved during restack; nothing published' (:102-103). Message text unchanged for the latter; the former reads 'task head changed on GitHub; synchronize before restacking'.
- `RestackStaleLocal`: GitHub's head equals `expected` but the local `refs/heads/<branch>` is missing or differs (the second half of :72-73; a failing `rev-parse` of a missing ref is this case, not a generic error). Message: 'local task ref is not the expected head; synchronize before restacking'.
- `RestackConflict`: the `git rebase --onto <new_base> <boundary>` step (:99) fails. That step stops using `git()` (which goes through `fm_binding.command`, whose error keeps only the first 500 bytes of stderr, bin/lib/fm_binding.py:11-16) and runs `subprocess.run(['git', '-C', tree, '-c', 'core.hooksPath=/dev/null', 'rebase', '--onto', new_base, boundary], stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)` itself, so the full stderr is available; a non-zero exit raises `RestackConflict('rebase conflict restacking onto <target>: ' + <last non-empty line of the full stderr>)`, which with real git is the 'Could not apply <sha>... <subject>' line. bin/lib/fm_binding.py is not changed. The temporary worktree is still removed by the existing `finally` (:144-145) and nothing is pushed.
- `RestackPublished`: every failure from just after the `push --force-with-lease` succeeded (:115-116) up to the `return` (:141): wrap that whole span so any `ValueError`, `KeyError`, `OSError` or `subprocess.SubprocessError` (including `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` from `gh pr edit` through `fm_binding.command`, a `remote_head` failure at :122, the `git` calls at :126-131 and the tracking `fetch` at :133) is re-raised as `RestackPublished` carrying the published head, e.g. 'task head published as <head>; ...: <original message>'. The existing specific texts stay: the retarget failure (:117-121), 'remote moved after publication' (:123-124) and 'remote updated but local tree changed' (:125-127). The `release_parent` failure stays caught as today (it only records 'cleanup deferred').
- `RestackPushUnknown` (exit 71): the `push --force-with-lease` call (:115-116) itself fails or times out. GitHub may or may not have accepted the ref (a dropped connection or `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` from `fm_binding.command`'s 120 s limit can come after the update), so the helper does not guess: it raises `RestackPushUnknown('push outcome unknown for <branch> (expected old head <expected>): ' + <error>)`, wrapping `ValueError`, `OSError` and `subprocess.SubprocessError` from that one call. Its cleanup follows the rule below (the push was attempted, so a cleanup failure cannot replace it).
- Output after publication: in `main()`, the `print(json.dumps(restack(...)))` (:190-191) is split so that `restack()` returns first; if writing its result then raises `OSError`, `main()` exits 69 with 'fm-stack: restack published; result output failed: <error>', never 65.
- Cleanup never hides a publication or an unknown push: track `push_attempted = True` immediately before the push call. The `finally` cleanup (`git(root, 'worktree', 'remove', '--force', tree)`, :143-144) is wrapped so that, once `push_attempted` is true, a cleanup failure never raises: it is appended to the in-flight `RestackPublished` or `RestackPushUnknown` message (keeping exit 69 or 71), or, on success, reported in the returned dict as `'tree_cleanup': '<error>'`. The `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(...)` at :95 is replaced by `directory = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='restack-', dir=scratch)` followed immediately by an outer `try:` that encloses everything from the `git worktree add` call (:97) to the end of the existing inner `try/finally`, whose own `finally` runs `shutil.rmtree(directory, ignore_errors=True)`; so the directory is removed on every path, including a failed `worktree add` (as `TemporaryDirectory` did), and its removal can never raise; both exist in Python 3.9, the baseline declared at design/design.md:3266, so no baseline change is needed (no `ignore_cleanup_errors`, which is 3.10+). Before the push is attempted, a cleanup failure behaves as today (a plain refusal, exit 65), because nothing was pushed.
- `RestackHeld`: the live-worker refusal in `main()` (:186-189), message unchanged ('task has a live worker; restack held').
`main()`'s handler (:194-199) maps, before the generic clause: `RestackConflict` → exit 66, `RestackMoved` → 67, `RestackStaleLocal` → 68, `RestackPublished` → 69, `RestackPushUnknown` → 71, `RestackHeld` → 75. Every other refusal (policy, protected branch, invalid target, protection unknown, merged parent head changed, dirty managed worktree, select errors, KeyError/OSError/SubprocessError) still exits 65 with the same 'fm-stack: ' stderr line. `select` is unchanged. bin/lib/fm-restack.sh passes the exit status through unchanged (it ends with `fm_stack restack ...` under `set -e`); its own 64/70 exits are unchanged, and `fm_stack`'s `return 65` when the repository cannot be resolved (bin/lib/fm-stack.sh:25) stays 65.

Autopilot restack without the ledger. `restack(pr, parent)` (bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:393-403) keeps its task/merged_at guard and its policy hold (the `restack-held-<number>` wake, unchanged). Then, with `number, head = str(pr['number']), pr['head']['sha']`:
1. Settled: see the record rule at the end of this item (no command).
2. Active work holds silently, exactly as `sync_branch`/`update_branch` do (fm_autopilot_branches.py:91-92, :131-132): `if self.round_live(task) or self.busy(task): return` before any command, with no record, retry or wake.
3. `token = f'restack:{number}:{head}'`; `if not self.retry_due(token): return`.
4. Write-ahead per head: before the command, set `data['restacks'][number] = dict(head=head, parent=parent['number'], task=task, outcome='started')` and `save()`. Then run the same argv as today (`self.script('lib/fm-restack.sh', '--pr', number, '--parent', parent['number'], '--expected-head', head)`, which keeps `--repo`/`--project`) through `self.probe` (exit status, stdout, stderr), not `self.command`. `line` is the last non-empty stderr line (or 'command failed'). Outcome handling:
   - `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` from `probe` is ambiguous (the helper may have pushed): the 'started' record stays and one wake is queued at once, identity `restack-interrupted-<number>-<head>`, en '<task> #<number> restack outcome unknown (timed out or interrupted); reconcile before review', zh-TW '<task> #<number> 重新堆疊結果不明（逾時或中斷）；審查前請先核對'.
   - Any other exception from `probe` (`OSError`: the process did not start) deletes the 'started' record and is a generic failure (step 10).
   - Only the statuses whose meaning is known replace the 'started' record: 0 (done), 69 (published), and the pre-push statuses 64, 65, 66, 67, 68, 70 and 75, which this task guarantees are produced before the push was attempted (a failure of the push call itself exits 71, every failure after a successful push exits 69, output after return exits 69, and cleanup cannot mask either). Exit 71 (push outcome unknown) is ambiguous: the 'started' record stays and the `restack-interrupted-<number>-<head>` wake is queued once. Any other status (a signal, shown as a negative status or 128+n, or 1 from an uncaught exception's traceback, or anything unlisted) is ambiguous exactly like a timeout: the 'started' record stays and the `restack-interrupted-<number>-<head>` wake is queued once.
   A 'started' record found at the start of a later `restack()` call (same `parent`, any head), meaning the autopilot was killed mid-command or the command timed out, makes `restack()` queue that same `restack-interrupted-<number>-<recorded head>` wake (deduplicated by identity) and return without running the helper. So an interrupted run holds for firstmate's reconciliation instead of re-running the rebase from the published head. Because `restack()` is only called while the child's base is still the merged parent (fm_autopilot.py:505-513), an interruption after the retarget succeeded would never reach that check, so `recover()` (fm_autopilot.py:239-243, run by `serve()` at startup, :729) also sweeps `data['restacks']`: for every record with `outcome='started'` it queues the same `restack-interrupted-<number>-<recorded head>` wake, naming the record's own `task` field (deduplicated by identity through `queue()`, so restarts never stack wakes), whatever the PR's current base. This is the only change to `recover()`; its `data['actions']` loop is unchanged.
5. Exit 0: `data['restacks'][number] = dict(head=head, parent=parent['number'], task=task, outcome='done')`, drop the retry token, save.
6. Exit 75 (live worker): delete the 'started' record and return silently; no retry change, no wake (the next poll tries again).
7. Exit 67 (moved): re-read GitHub before trusting it, with `self.command(self.gh('pr', 'view', number, '--repo', self.ctx['repository'], '--json', 'headRefOid'))` (no ETag cache, as update_branch does at :153-158). If that read succeeds and its `headRefOid` differs from `head`: set the record to `outcome='moved'` (same head, parent and task), drop the retry token, no wake. If it equals `head` or the read fails: treat as a generic failure (step 10), so a disagreement never goes silent.
8. Exit 66 (rebase conflict): set the record to `outcome='conflict'` (same head, parent and task), drop the retry token and queue one wake at once, identity `restack-conflict-<number>-<head>`, en '<task> #<number> restack hit a rebase conflict; resolve by hand: <line>', zh-TW '<task> #<number> 重新堆疊遇到 rebase 衝突；需手動處理：<line>'.
9. Exit 69 (published but incomplete): set the record to `outcome='published'` (same head, parent and task), drop the retry token and queue one wake at once, identity `restack-published-<number>-<head>`, en '<task> #<number> restack published but did not finish; synchronize and finish before review: <line>', zh-TW '<task> #<number> 重新堆疊已發布但未完成；請同步並完成後再審查：<line>'. Because the push already moved GitHub's head, the autopilot then holds: while `data['restacks'][number]` has `outcome='published'` and the same `parent`, `restack()` returns before step 2 at any head, so it never repeats the rebase, push or retarget and never queues a second wake for this PR; finishing is firstmate's (the wake says so). The record outlives head changes (see `prune_branches` below) and ends only when the PR is terminal; once firstmate completes the retarget the child's base is no longer the merged parent, so `restack()` is not called again.
10. Exit 68 (stale local ref), 64, 65 or 70, or a step-7 disagreement: delete the 'started' record, then `self.branch_failure('restack', number, head, task, line)`, giving attempts at poll offsets 0, 1 and 3 and one wake on the third failure ('<task> #<number> restack failed after 3 attempts: <line>'). For 68, `sync_branch` (run in the same `pull()` at :424 for every open PR) fast-forwards the local ref between attempts, so a stale local branch either heals or wakes; it never stalls silently.
No `once()` entry is written for restack. `data['restacks']` gets a default `{}` in `Pilot.__init__`'s setdefault list (:63-65). `prune_branches` (fm_autopilot_branches.py:13-22) also prunes `data['restacks']`: a terminal PR (`head is None`) drops the record; a head change drops it unless its `outcome` is 'published' or 'started' (those holds must survive the head the push itself may have created). Retry tokens are pruned as today. Step 1 is: if the record has the same `parent` and `outcome` 'published', return; if it has the same `parent` and `outcome` 'started', queue the interrupted wake (above) and return; otherwise if it has the same `head` and `parent`, return. Every `data['restacks']` record carries exactly four fields: `head`, `parent`, `task` (from `self.task(pr)` at the time it is written) and `outcome`.

Migration. A one-time `migrated_t204` upgrade in `Pilot.__init__`, after the `migrated_t200` block (fm_autopilot.py:85-98) and before `serve()` calls `recover()`, mirroring `migrated_t193`: delete every `data['actions']` entry whose `identity[0] == 'restack'` in any state, and drop from `data['wakes']` the undelivered `autopilot-`+key([project, 'action-'+token]) wake of each; delivered files under state/wake-queue/ stay byte-identical and nothing is requeued. `data['restacks']` starts empty, so a merged-parent child with a live policy is attempted again on the next poll after upgrade (guarded by the expected-head lease, the worker lock and steps 1-4). A legacy restack action in state 'started' or 'uncertain' cannot exist here (none in today's state, and stacking is held in this repository); the migration still drops it rather than translating it, because its fingerprint does not record the parent. `once()`, `recover()` and `data['actions']` remain for the last ledger class (launch-review); deleting them is step L3, not this task.

Tests, all under tests/** (files stay under 1200 lines: autopilot_cases.py is 770, stacking_cases.py 266):
- tests/stacking_cases.py, existing tests: `test_restack_uses_parent_boundary_and_expected_lease` (:170-201) and `test_restack_preserves_dirty_managed_worktree` (:203-228) reach the rebase, which no longer goes through the mocked `git`; both patch `stack.subprocess.run` so the rebase argv returns exit 0 (other argv are not expected there), and the success test asserts that argv exactly: `['git', '-C', <tree>, '-c', 'core.hooksPath=/dev/null', 'rebase', '--onto', <base>, <boundary>]` in place of its current mocked-git assertion at :197. The dirty test then still raises its 'dirty' ValueError before any push.
- tests/stacking_cases.py, new tests: `restack()` raises `RestackMoved` when `remote_head` returns a different headRefOid (and never calls `git rev-parse refs/heads/...`); `RestackStaleLocal` when GitHub matches but the patched `git` answers a different SHA for `rev-parse refs/heads/<branch>`, and also when that `rev-parse` raises; `RestackConflict` when the rebase subprocess (patch `stack.subprocess.run` for the rebase argv only) returns exit 1 with stderr recorded from a real `git rebase --onto` conflict whose commit subject is long enough that the stderr exceeds 500 bytes (record it by running git in a temporary repo); the exception message ends with the full 'Could not apply <sha>... <subject>' line, unclipped, and no `push` call is made; no `restack-*` directory left under the scratch dir when the patched `git` raises on `worktree add` (the refusal is still a plain ValueError) nor after a successful restack; `RestackPushUnknown` (still, with the cleanup error appended) when the patched `git` raises on the `push` call and also on `worktree remove`; `RestackPushUnknown` when the patched `git` raises on the `push` call, both with a `ValueError` carrying git's real 'failed to push some refs' text and with `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, with no retarget (`command`) call afterwards; `main()` exiting 69 when writing the result raises `OSError` after `restack()` returned (patch `restack` to return a dict and `print`/`sys.stdout` to raise); `RestackPublished` (still) when the retarget fails after the push and the patched `git` also raises on `worktree remove` in the `finally`, with the cleanup error appended to the message, and a successful restack whose `worktree remove` raises still returns its result with a `tree_cleanup` field; `RestackPublished` when `command` (the `gh pr edit` retarget) raises after the push, and also when `remote_head` raises `KeyError` on its post-push read (:122) and when `command` raises `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` for the retarget: each message names the published head; `RestackMoved` for the in-flight 'child moved during restack' case. Each also satisfies `isinstance(error, ValueError)`.
- tests/stacking-restack.test.sh: the live-worker case (:41) now expects 75 (message unchanged); the held-policy case (:18) stays 65. Add an entrypoint case with stacking allowed, no lock held, and a `gh pr view` stub answering the real JSON shape with `headRefOid` 'c'*40 for `--expected-head` 'b'*40: exit 67 and stderr containing 'task head changed on GitHub'.
- tests/lib/autopilot_branch_fixture.py: `branch_probe` answers an argv whose first element ends with 'lib/fm-restack.sh' with a configurable `self.restack_answer` (rc, stdout, stderr), default `(0, '{"head": ...}', '')`, set in `branch_setup`; the existing `assert argv[0] == 'git'` stays for everything else.
- tests/lib/autopilot_cases.py: adapt `test_stacking_requires_confirmed_force_policy_and_expected_head` (:142-152) to find the argv among probe calls (same assertions on `--expected-head`, HEAD and `--project`). New cases with policy allowed: exit 0 records exactly `dict(head=HEAD, parent=<parent>, task='T-001', outcome='done')` and a second poll at the same head runs no command; `round_live`/`busy` true runs no command and leaves no record, retry or wake; exit 75 leaves no record and no wake and retries next poll; exit 67 with `gh pr view` answering another head records 'moved' with no wake and no retry, and with `gh pr view` answering the same head enters the retry series; exit 66 queues exactly one 'rebase conflict' wake and runs no further command at that head; a probe raising `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` leaves the 'started' record and queues exactly one 'outcome unknown' wake, and later polls (at the same head and at a new head) run no helper and queue no second wake; a 'started' record left by a killed autopilot (written, then the pilot restarted without an outcome) holds and wakes once the same way after restart; `recover()` with a 'started' restack record whose PR base is no longer the merged parent queues exactly one interrupted wake whose task is the record's `task` (assert the queued wake's `task` and its line '<task> #<number> restack outcome unknown…'), and a second restart followed by `recover()` and `flush()` queues no second wake; a probe raising `OSError` deletes the record and enters the retry series; exit 71 (push outcome unknown), exit 1 and exit -9 (a killed helper) each keep the 'started' record, queue exactly one 'outcome unknown' wake and run no helper on later polls; exit 69 queues exactly one 'published but did not finish' wake, and further polls at the new (published) head with the base still the merged parent, with `sync_branch` answering either way, run no restack command and queue no second wake; the 'published' record survives `prune_branches` at the new head and is dropped when the PR closes; exit 68 and exit 65 run at poll offsets 0, 1 and 3 only and queue one wake naming the last stderr line; a new head (prune) clears the record and attempts again; no `data['actions']` entry is ever written. Migration: legacy restack actions in started, done and uncertain states with queued wakes are removed with their undelivered wakes, one delivered wake file stays byte-identical, a launch-review action survives, and two restarts each followed by `recover()` and `flush()` leave identical state.
- The two existing migration tests that use a restack action as the surviving example (`test_event_recheck_migration_removes_all_states_before_recovery_once` :636-685 and `test_advance_migration_removes_all_states_before_recovery_once` :687-718) switch that example to a launch-review identity, so no test asserts restack ledger semantics. (They would stay green unchanged, because `migrated_t204` is set at first start, but they must not describe a class no code writes.)

Docs, edited in place (T-189 rule; nothing appended at the end of design.md):
- design/design.md §15.8 'Pilot and advanced integration', the sentence 'The remaining write-ahead classes are restack and review launch under `state/autopilot/`...' (about :5340-5342): review launch is the remaining write-ahead class; restack keeps a per-PR-head record in `restacks` with the outcomes above, and `migrated_t204` drops legacy restack actions and their undelivered wakes.
- design/design.md §15.8 subsection '#### T-143: operating a stack' (about :5358-5395): one paragraph after the helper description listing the helper's exit statuses (0 done, 65 refusal, 66 rebase conflict, 67 GitHub head moved, 68 local task ref stale, 69 published but unfinished, 71 push outcome unknown, 75 live worker) and what the autopilot does with each (silent for 67 confirmed by a fresh read and for 75; immediate wake for 66 and 69; retries at 0/1/3 then one wake for 64, 65, 68 and 70; an 'outcome unknown' wake and a hold for 71, a timeout, a kill or any other status; at startup every unfinished restack record wakes once). A 'published' or 'started' hold lasts, across heads, until the PR closes or firstmate finishes the restack by hand (which moves the child's base off the merged parent, so the autopilot no longer restacks it).
- docs/autopilot.md, the paragraph ending 'The remaining write-ahead classes are restack and review launch; interrupted actions remain held for reconciliation.' (about :71-72): same facts in the doc's own wording.

Callers and mirrors (grep of 'restack' over bin/, tests/, docs/, design/design.md, skills/, board/): `fm-restack.sh` is called only by `Pilot.restack` and by the operator command shown in design T-143; `fm_stack.py restack` only by `fm-restack.sh`; `fm_stack select` callers (fm-dispatch.sh, fm-worker.sh via bin/lib/fm-stack.sh) are unaffected. tests/option-loop.test.sh (:64 'fm-restack 5', :108) counts flags only and stays green unchanged. bin/fm-worker.sh:1009 only names the helper in a message and is unchanged. No board, i18n or event type changes; the new wakes reuse `queue()` (no new fm-emit type, so fm-diagram.sh needs nothing).

Scope boundary and overlap. No change to `once()`, jobs, or to `recover()` beyond the restack sweep in acceptance 3, launch-review, `advance`, `sync_branch`, `update_branch`, `serve()`, `live()`, `ensure`, `owner.json`, bin/fm-autopilot.sh or bin/lib/fm_stack.py's `select`/`release_parent`. T-203 (autopilot reload and drain) is specified in parallel and edits `serve`/`live`/`ensure`/`owner.json` in bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py and bin/fm-autopilot.sh, and likely design §15.8 and docs/autopilot.md; the two must merge one after the other, the second branch-updated onto the first. T-204 does not touch those functions; if T-203 lands first and adds its own migration flag, the `migrated_t204` block goes after it.

In flight. Nothing in flight edits bin/lib/fm_stack.py, fm-restack.sh or the restack path (T-200 and T-199 have merged; T-203 is not dispatched). Today's autopilot state holds no restack action (only 2 launch-review actions, both 'done'), and this repository has no CONVENTIONS.md, so stacking is held and `restack()` only ever queues the policy-hold wake here; `migrated_t204` therefore removes nothing today. The running autopilot keeps its old snapshot until replaced (`fm-autopilot.sh ensure` exits early while a service runs, bin/fm-autopilot.sh:51-53): after this merges firstmate stops the service and runs `bin/fm-autopilot.sh ensure --all` (until T-203 automates it), and `migrated_t204` runs at that start.

Workers do not run the suites. Evidence is the required GitHub check and the six gates. Fail-first is expected from tests/autopilot.test.sh (autopilot_cases.py: the new restack outcome, hold, retry and migration cases are red on base, where restack uses `once()`/`command`), tests/stacking.test.sh (stacking_cases.py: the new exception-class cases are red on base, where those classes do not exist) and tests/stacking-restack.test.sh (exit 75 for the live worker and the new exit-67 entrypoint case are red on base, where both exit 65). The adapted `test_stacking_requires_confirmed_force_policy...` case and the two migration-example switches are regression guards. Stubs answer like the real tools: `gh pr view --json headRefOid` returns that JSON object, and the rebase-conflict stderr is recorded from a real git run.
